newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lufthansa boss issues plea against strikes.
newsitem.headline: Lufthansa boss issues plea against strikes.

text.p: The head of German airline Deutsche Lufthansa AG has issued a personal plea to some 50,000 workers not to vote for an all-out strike in their pay dispute with the flag carrier.

In a letter to staff obtained by Reuters on Tuesday, chairman Juergen Weber said the airline still wanted to create more jobs in Germany despite a cost-cutting programme worth more than 500 million marks ($302 million) and plans for increased cooperation with other airlines.

"I am appealing to you personally because of two concerns: one, the threat of commercial damages, and two, an apparent lack of confidence among your ranks in the management," Weber said in a letter sent out late last week.
Ballotting of Lufthansa staff by the white-collar worker union DAG started on Tuesday and is due to end on February 25.

Dag, which organised two limited walk-outs by staff late last year that cost Lufthansa tens of millions of marks in lost business, needs the support of 70 percent of its members at the airline for a full strike.

In his letter, Weber listed a number of powerful rivals that were stepping up competition against Lufthansa. They include a proposed British Airways -American Airlines link-up and a number of other European airlines entering the German market.
"Others are wanting to take more and more slices of the bread, on which we live," Weber warned.
He said the competitive situation faced by the airline, and the management's reaction to it, had not been accurately portayed by DAG.

In particular, he promised that ancillary services for the airline "should, where possible, be provided by Lufthansa staff", playing down fears that the airline was seeking to contract out more and more of its service activities.

Lufthansa is offering DAG workers, which include ground-, air- and cockpit staff, a one-off payment of 33 percent of a month's salary and a payment of 500 marks cash or 625 marks in Lufthansa shares. A similar wage deal has already been signed with the OeTV public sector and transport union.
DAG wants a pay rise of around four percent and is unhappy with the duration of the 27-month contract that Lufthansa wants its workers to sign.
